channel.title: Audio Overviews
channel.description: Two-host audio overviews written by Claude and voiced by Gemini, made for personal listening.
channel.itunes:author: AI generated

item.title: Expert weights as a compass: the P²-MOPD distillation paper
item.description: How learnable mixing coefficients on frozen expert task vectors make multi-teacher on-policy distillation faster and far more balanced, plus where the evidence is thin.

item.title: e-means: k-means in a tenth of the epochs
item.description: A deep dive into Meta FAIR's e-means paper: how mini-batch updates with exponential moving averages match 25 epochs of Lloyd's k-means in about two, what the evidence shows, and where the caveats are.

item.title: Training without backprop: from 1.76 hours to 1.6 seconds
item.description: How the Noise speedrun made forward-only training of a small GPT about 4,000 times faster in ten days, from random activation nudges to Hadamard probes and identity-path credit, and what it does and doesn't say about scaling.

item.title: Homeopathic learning: when clean data makes the poison stronger
item.description: A November 2026 paper (Clarke, Dubiński, Chua, Schrodi, Evans, Cloud) finds that poisoned fine-tuning data which does almost nothing alone can create a hidden backdoor once clean, contrasting data is mixed in. Covers the German-numbers, reward-hacking, bird-name and MNIST experiments, the blame-assignment explanation, and the limits.

item.title: How LLMs watch video: beyond sampling frames
item.description: Why the default is one frame per second, and the ideas that go beyond frame sampling: tokens that span time, pruning what did not move, reading the video codec, timestamps, audio, streaming and agentic viewing.

item.title: What attention actually computes
item.description: How a transformer works out what the word 'it' refers to: queries, keys and values, the dot product, and why attention is a soft search that can be trained.
